messages.content: Can you help me find restaurants in New York, NY that cater to my dietary preferences which include Vegan, Gluten-free and Dairy-free options, and then do the same for Los Angeles, CA and Chicago, IL?

function.name: restaurant_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby restaurants based on specific dietary preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Los Angeles, CA

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find restaurants in New York, NY that cater to their dietary preferences: Vegan, Gluten-free, Dairy-free. Then do the same for Los Angeles, CA and Chicago, IL.

We have a function `restaurant_find_nearby` that can locate nearby restaurants based on specific dietary preferences. It takes arguments: location (string), dietary_preference optional array of strings with default ["Vegan"]. The function returns any.

We need to call this function for each city: New York, NY; Los Angeles, CA; Chicago, IL. We need to pass dietary_preference as ["Vegan", "Gluten-free", "Dairy-free"].

We should call the function three times. According to guidelines, we should not provide any other text besides the function calls. So we will produce three separate function calls. Each call should be a separate JSON object with name and arguments. The assistant should output them sequentially. No additional text.

Thus we will produce:

{
"name": "restaurant_find_nearby",
"arguments": {
"location": "New York, NY",
"dietary_preference": ["Vegan", "Gluten-free", "Dairy-free"]
}
}

Then next for Los Angeles, CA. Then Chicago, IL.

We should ensure correct JSON formatting. Also note that the function expects "dietary_preference" as an array of strings. The type says "dietary_preference?: "Vegan" | "Vegetarian" | "Gluten-free" | "Dairy-free" | "Nut-free"[], // default: ["Vegan"]". That seems like a mistake: it says "dietary_preference?: "Vegan" | "Vegetarian" | "Gluten-free" | "Dairy-free" | "Nut-free"[]". But we interpret that as an array of those strings. So we pass an array.

Thus we produce three calls.
